title: Stars and Brokers: Knowledge Spillovers Among Medical Scientists
near_miss_reason: Fixed-effects Poisson quasi-maximum-likelihood (xtpqml, nonlinear model) in every reported column (Tables 2-8, Figures 3-4; article text: 'conditional quasi-maximum likelihood Poisson specification' in every table note); every column also enters a 'post' main effect that switches on for the matched control coauthors at the pseudo-death year (extra treatment regressor) and career-age-category fixed effects (additional additive fixed effects); the headline columns add continuous post x brokerage interactions (treatment-by-characteristic interactions). Staggered binary design: star deaths at star-specific years 1965-2009, coauthors of matched living stars as never-treated controls, coauthor-link id and year FE; the analysis panel is shipped.
eligible_reason: The design is a staggered binary DiD (coauthors of star scientists who die in different years, 1965-2009, versus coauthors of matched living stars), but every reported column is a fixed-effects Poisson quasi-maximum-likelihood regression (xtpqml), which the protocol excludes as a nonlinear model. In addition every column includes a 'post' main effect (a pseudo-death post indicator that switches on for control coauthors as well, i.e. an additional staggered regressor), career-age-category fixed effects (additional additive FE), and in most columns continuous post x brokerage interactions. No linear TWFE column exists, so the paper is not eligible and not classed as a near-miss under the controls/extra-regressor definition; it would become a near-miss only if Poisson DiD were admitted.
design_notes: Unit id = group(star_id author_id coauthor_id): a coauthor (author_id) linked to a star (star_id) through a coauthorship; panel years 1965-2009, rectangularised to event time in [-40, 40] (D1_creating_panel_scientists.do lines 77-115). treated = 1 if the star died (705 deceased stars, 20,424 ids), 0 for coauthors of 722 matched living stars (20,363 ids) who are assigned the matched star's death year (D2_analysis.do lines 25-51). post = (year > death); posttreated = post x treated; z_brokerage = brokerage degree standardized at time 0; post_broker = post x z_brokerage; posttreated_broker = posttreated x z_brokerage (D1 lines 150-162). Outcomes: pub_y (annual publication count), pub_cites_y_w5 (JIF-weighted publications), pub_nostar_y / pub_w_nostar_y (publications without the star). Main estimator (Table 2, D2_analysis.do lines 78-86): xi: xtpqml y post posttreated [post_broker posttreated_broker] i.age_cat i.year if career_age<40, fe i(id) cluster(author_id). Figure 3: brokerage-decile interactions; Figure 4: binned event-time (5-year bins, -20..+20) by brokerage quartile, again xtpqml with age_cat and year FE. Tables 3-8 and appendix tables add further post x characteristic interactions, alternative brokerage measures, sudden-death and Azoulay subsamples, and a placebo with random death years (Table G3 col 2).
estimators_reported: poisson_fe_qml_did (xtpqml with id FE, year FE, age-category FE, cluster author_id)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Star deaths span 1965-2009 (sample restricted to year 1965-2009 and |time| <= 40), so there are many death-year cohorts; the exact count requires tabulating death among treated ids in panel_scientists.dta (not run).

data_files: B_death/*.sqlite3, causes_death.csv; A_Publications/JCR_2017.csv, scimagojr.csv, mesh.RData (construction inputs)
data_files_note: The analysis panel is shipped in full (README: everything needed for D2_analysis.do). Raw Medline/Author-ity inputs for the construction steps are external. README notes D2_analysis.do takes about 21 hours to run.
software_notes: Stata/MP 15.1 for the panel build (D1) and all regressions (D2: xtpqml, parmest, esttab, mmerge); R 3.1.2 for publication/network construction (A, B, C folders); Neo4j for the coauthorship network.
priority_note: Design qualifies (staggered star deaths, never-treated matched controls, data shipped) but no linear TWFE column is reported: all columns are FE Poisson with a post main effect and age-category FE.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). The regression list data/packages/mnsc.2021.4032_regressions.txt is empty, presumably because the extraction pipeline did not recognise 'xi: xtpqml'. Flag for the lead: if the project decides to admit Poisson DiD or to construct linear counterparts, Table 2 columns 2 and 4 (y on post + posttreated with id, year and age_cat FE, career_age<40, cluster author_id) are the natural candidates; the linear version would still need to drop the post main effect and the age_cat FE to satisfy the protocol.
hand_check_nov4: Near-miss (nonlinear Poisson in every column; post main effect; age-category FE). The screener left near_miss false because Poisson was not in the controls/extra-regressor definition, but the near-miss taxonomy (code/20 'Nonlinear model' category; PROTOCOL coding rule) covers it: staggered binary design with unit and year FE, no linear column. Article text confirms the Poisson QML specification in all tables. Not controls-only.
